item.title: In Trump’s Washington, Ballooning National Debt Stirs Little Action
item.description: The relative indifference to the news that the U.S. government now owes $40 trillion demonstrates how drastically the politics of deficit spending has changed.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:description: A sign showing the national debt last week at a bus stop in Washington.

item.title: Survivors of Nepal Flood Left in Stunned Disbelief: ‘They All Died, and I Lived’
item.description: A visit near the border with Tibet laid bare the effects of a swollen river’s furious speed. Miles of devastation were left behind in a flash flood that killed more than 300.
item.dc:creator: Anupreeta Das and Atul Loke
item.media:description: Residents waiting to be airlifted by helicopter in the Rasuwa district of Nepal.

item.title: Climate Change Raises Risk of Disasters Like Nepal Floods
item.description: Glaciers and permafrost in the Himalayas are melting faster as temperatures rise, though scientists are still studying the exact causes of this week’s landslide.
item.dc:creator: Maxine Joselow and Leo Sands
item.media:credit: Atul Loke for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mud-laden water and debris surges through the widened channel of the Bhotekoshi River in the northern Rasuwa district of Nepal, on Thursday.

item.title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
item.description: The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic, led by Dario Amodei, was barred from government work after it insisted that its technology not be used in mass surveillance of Americans or for autonomous lethal weapons.

item.title: Trump Plans to Mark 9/11 at the Pentagon, Not Ground Zero
item.description: President Trump originally intended to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Sept. 11 with remarks at ground zero, but the memorial’s organizers do not allow speeches. Mr. Trump changed his plans.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman, Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Dana Rubinstein and Sally Goldenberg
item.media:description: Memorials left at the south tower reflecting pool last year at the World Trade Center in Manhattan.

item.title: Judge Says Trump’s Name Should Stay Off Kennedy Center for Now
item.description: After the court forced the removal of the president’s name from the building’s title, the center devised a plan to add an inscription honoring President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague and Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: Though President Trump’s name was taken down weeks ago, the scaffolding and tarps used in the process remain up outside the Kennedy Center.

item.title: Trump Administration to Expand Deportation Flights to Haiti
item.description: Flights to the Caribbean nation will increase from once a month to once a week now that the Supreme Court allowed President Trump to cancel a humanitarian program.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Aleaziz, Zolan Kanno-Youngs and Frances Robles
item.media:description: Deportation flights to Haiti will increase as soon as this week.

item.title: Judge Once Again Bars Postal Service From Restricting Mail-In Vote
item.description: After reviewing the agency’s final plan to comply with President Trump’s demands, a federal judge barred the Postal Service from imposing new restrictions on mail-in voting.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: In a filing on Thursday, the Postal Service denied that its proposal left any room for it to second-guess states on which voters were eligible to cast a ballot.

item.title: Progressives Condemn Pick of Pro-Israel Democrat Atop House Panel
item.description: Outrage over making Representative Jared Moskowitz, who is vocally pro-Israel, the top Democrat on a Middle East policy subcommittee reflected the party’s rift over Israel.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:description: On Tuesday, Representative Jared Moskowitz of Florida, a vocally pro-Israel Democrat, was chosen to serve as the ranking member on a key subcommittee with jurisdiction over Middle East policy.

item.title: LA Mayor Karen Bass Eases Street Vending Crackdown After Debate
item.description: Mayor Karen Bass had compared the ubiquitous purveyors of street food with homeless encampments. Her opponent, Nithya Raman, said vendors should be brought into the system.
item.dc:creator: Livia Albeck-Ripka
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: A street vendor in the Boyle Heights neighborhood in Los Angeles.

item.title: ‘Intrinsic Capacity’: The Most Important Longevity Term You’ve Never Heard Of
item.description: Intrinsic capacity is quickly becoming a preferred way to measure and assess human aging.
item.dc:creator: Dana G. Smith

item.title: C.I.A. Chief Delivered Bleak Assessment of Russia’s War in Secretive Moscow Visit
item.description: John Ratcliffe’s meeting this week with a Russian intelligence chief was aimed at pushing the Kremlin to pursue a peace deal with Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Adam Entous and Julian E. Barnes
item.media:description: John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, delivered an urgent message to Aleksandr V. Bortnikov, the head of Russia’s F.S.B. intelligence service this week in a secret visit to Moscow.

item.title: Yielding on French Could Restart Trade Talks, Canadian Officials Say
item.description: Canada’s minister in charge of trade with the U.S. was responding to comments by Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative. But that was before any mention of Lake Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen and Vjosa Isai
item.media:description: Dominic LeBlanc, Canada’s minister responsible for trade with the United States, center, with Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada.

item.title: Trump Signs Executive Order to Rename Lake Ontario to Lake America
item.description: The president also reiterated his criticism that Canada “treats us very badly.” Trade talks between the nations collapsed last week.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times

item.title: Canada Hires U.S. Scholars From Harvard and Other Top Universities
item.description: A crackdown on American academia by the Trump administration has handed Canadian universities a rare opportunity to lure some top researchers north.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Nasuna Stuart-Ulin for The New York Times
item.media:description: McGill University in Montreal is one of the schools that has benefited from the Canada-bound brain drain from U.S. institutions.

item.title: How SSENSE, a Canadian Retailer, Is Grappling With Trump’s Tariffs
item.description: Ssense’s comeback efforts include moving a core part of its business to the United States so American customers can avoid hefty tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Peter Eavis
item.media:credit: Nasuna Stuart-Ulin for The New York Times
item.media:description: A stylist prepared a rack of clothes at a Ssense store in Montreal. The company, an online clothes retailer, is trying to lessen the burden of U.S. tariffs on its business.

item.title: Inside the Iceland Eclipse Festival: $1,000-a-Week Yurts and Endless Optimism
item.description: At a festival on a disc golf course, on a peninsula in Iceland, waiting for the sky to descend into darkness.
item.dc:creator: Callie Holtermann and Lexi Parra

item.title: Near-Total Lunar Eclipse Will Turn Moon Blood Red
item.description: People in the Americas, Africa and Europe will have a chance to see Earth’s shadow create a near-total blood moon.
item.dc:creator: Katrina Miller
item.media:description: Moon gazers in South America and the eastern half of North America will be able to see an entire eclipse on Thursday night as long as clouds don’t interfere.

item.title: In ‘9 to 5,’ Dolly Parton Put a Friendly Face on Feminism
item.description: In 1980, feminists were often stereotyped as man-hating or out of touch. Then Parton gave the movement a boost — and an anthem.
item.dc:creator: Susan Dominus

item.title: Fans Push to Rename Nashville Airport for Dolly Parton
item.description: A surging online push to rename Nashville International Airport for the beloved Tennessean superstar could get snagged in bureaucracy and politics.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung and Emily Cochrane
item.media:description: “Who doesn’t want to be ‘departin’ from Parton’?” said one of the fans behind an online petition to rename Nashville International Airport for Dolly Parton, who died on Tuesday.

item.title: On Night of Deadly Air Canada Crash, Two LaGuardia Controllers Left Early
item.description: The two controllers are among a dozen that the Federal Aviation Administration has taken steps to fire as part of an inquiry into timecard fraud, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:credit: Dakota Santiago for The New York Times
item.media:description: An Air Canada jet crashed into a fire truck in March, killing two people.

item.title: Gwyneth Paltrow’s Hamptons Dinner for Sam Altman Postponed
item.description: The actress and wellness entrepreneur did not deny her plans to host an intimate gathering for Sam Altman. But it will have to wait.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bernstein
item.media:credit: Jutharat Pinyodoonyachet for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gwyneth Paltrow at her home in Amagansett, N.Y. The actress and mogul was scheduled to host an event for OpenAI’s Sam Altman that has been postponed.

item.title: Climber Stranded for Hours on 6-Inch Rock Ledge Before Rescue
item.description: Racing against the darkness, rescuers in California on Saturday saved a man who had become stranded on a ledge perched atop a soaring peak on the Sierra Nevada.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
